text.p: German energy group RWE AG said on Wednesday it was in the final stages of talks on joining a telecommunications alliance with Veba AG and Cable & Wireless.
It also said it was quitting a grouping with British Telecom and Viag due to differences in market positioning over Germany's planned E2 mobile telephone network.

RWE said in a regulatory news announcement that it was "taking a new direction to enter the German telecommunications market". An announcement would be made later in the day after a supervisory board meeting.

The switch comes as Germany prepares to award the licence early next year for the E2 mobile phone network, the country's fourth, and competitors prepare the scrapping of Deutsche Telekom AG's market monopoly in 1998.
RWE said, however, it would continue to cooperate with VIAG in the area of telecoms infrastructure.
Veba already cooperates with Cable & Wireless through its telecommunications subsidiary Vebacom.
The announcement comes after RWE denied a newspaper report in April that it had re-opened negotiations with telecoms operators other than Viag and British Telekom.
Viag said it would go ahead with plans to make a joint application with BT the E2 mobile telephone licence despite the RWE pullout.
"The telecommunications strategy of Viag and BT will continue unchanged without the entry of RWE into the alliance," Viag said in a separate news release.
